title: Steward platform values, v1
description: The one operator input for a platform install. It holds the values that several charts must agree on: namespaces, service account identities, cluster addresses, TLS, the database, public origins, audiences and the SPIFFE trust domain. scripts/generate.sh combines it with bom/bom.json into per-chart values and helmfile inputs. Fields marked x-reserved belong to governed mode; they are part of the design so that the file does not change shape later, but the v1 generator rejects them until governed mode lands. The task-auth profile implements the fields it needs: the public Steward origin and issuer, the task API audience, the github-oidc-exchange namespace and service account, the edge and the exchange's own settings. The browser-admin profile adds Steward's Google Workspace browser login, its browser-auth egress CIDRs and its administration settings.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors.

environment.description: Environment name. It selects the helmfile environment and the output directory helmfile/generated/<environment>.

purpose.description: evaluation allows the evaluation-only pieces (in-cluster PostgreSQL, a self-signed CA). production forbids them: the operator supplies the database and the certificate issuer.

profile.description: Install profile from the BOM. The v1 generator implements core, task-auth and browser-admin (task-auth plus Steward's browser web UI and Google login).

cluster.description: Facts about the target cluster that chart values depend on.

domain.description: Cluster DNS domain. Service certificates and in-cluster URLs use it.

serviceAccountTokenAudience.description: Audience that this cluster's service account tokens carry, usually the service account issuer (kubectl get --raw /.well-known/openid-configuration). Steward's TokenReview must use it. It differs between distributions; on kind it is https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local.

dnsNamespace.description: Namespace of the cluster DNS pods. NetworkPolicy allows DNS egress to it.

kubeApi.description: How NetworkPolicy reaches the Kubernetes API. Charts take literal CIDRs only. Which address and port your CNI matches (service IP and 443, or endpoint IPs and 6443) depends on the CNI; see docs/prerequisites.md.

namespaces.description: Namespaces of every platform component. Other charts refer to these in NetworkPolicy, service URLs and workload identities, so they are set once here.

steward.description: Steward control plane. Evaluation PostgreSQL and the evaluation CA also go here.

certManager.description: cert-manager, when the reference install installs it.

identityExchange.description: github-oidc-exchange, and the policy ConfigMap and keyring Secret it reads. task-auth profile.

runners.description: steward-run runner scale set. Reserved for governed mode.

litellm.description: Inference proxy. Reserved for governed mode.

openshell.description: Sandbox gateway. Reserved for governed mode.

spire.description: SPIRE server and agents. Reserved for governed mode.

runtimes.description: Namespaces where agent runtimes run (PodSecurity privileged). Reserved for governed mode.

serviceAccounts.description: Workload identities. Service account names are fixed by the product charts; annotations (for example cloud workload identity) are set here so that the identities other components trust are defined in one place.

identityExchange.description: github-oidc-exchange. Its name is fixed by the chart. task-auth profile.

tls.description: How Steward's API and webhook get their service certificates, and how the webhook CA bundle is supplied.

mode.description: certManager: cert-manager issues both certificates and injects the webhook CA bundle. customerSecret: the operator creates both TLS Secrets and supplies the public CA bundle.

install.description: Install the BOM-pinned cert-manager. Set false when the cluster already runs cert-manager.

source.description: evaluation: the reference install creates a self-signed CA Issuer in the Steward namespace (evaluation purpose only). operator: use the operator's existing Issuer or ClusterIssuer named in ref.

kind.description: An Issuer must be in the Steward namespace.

apiSecretName.description: kubernetes.io/tls Secret for the API. Defaults to the chart's name.

webhookSecretName.description: kubernetes.io/tls Secret for the webhook. Defaults to the chart's name.

caBundleFile.description: Path to the public PEM CA bundle that verifies the webhook certificate, relative to this file. Never a private key.

source.description: evaluation: the reference install runs the BOM-pinned PostgreSQL in the Steward namespace, without TLS or persistence, and writes the database Secret (evaluation purpose only). operator: a separately operated PostgreSQL, at or above the BOM's dependencies.postgresql.minVersion; the operator creates the database Secret.

evaluationVersion.description: evaluation source only: the PostgreSQL version the reference install runs, as a major version ("17") or an exact one; it must name exactly one entry of the BOM's dependencies.postgresql.tested. Default: the BOM's default version.

secret.description: Secret in the Steward namespace whose key holds the database URL.

cidrs.description: Literal CIDRs of the database for NetworkPolicy egress. For evaluation on kind, the pod subnet.

tls.description: Database TLS. verify-full also needs the URL in the Secret to use sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/run/database-tls/ca.crt.

ca.description: Public CA that verifies the database server, in the Steward namespace.

artifacts.description: Where the product charts and images come from. Optional: without it, or with source bom, every product artifact is the BOM's upstream reference and the output is unchanged. source built takes each deployed product's chart and images from a built-artifacts lock instead: the products as the operator built them from source at the BOM's release commits and pushed them to their own registry, with their own digests (docs/fork-and-build.md). The generator checks the lock against the BOM and fails, listing each one, when a chart or image of a product the profile deploys is missing. Versions, values and profiles stay the BOM's, and so do the external dependencies and steward-run's projected release coordinates.

source.description: bom (the default): the BOM's upstream artifacts. built: the artifacts listed in builtLock.

builtLock.description: Path to the built-artifacts lock, a JSON file matching schemas/built-lock/v1.schema.json: absolute, or relative to this file. Required with source built, and only allowed with it.

networkPolicy.description: Cross-component NetworkPolicy inputs. Charts keep their NetworkPolicies on; these values open only what the platform needs.

apiserverIngressNamespaces.description: Namespaces whose pods may call the Steward API directly.

edgeNamespace.description: Namespace where the edge's data plane runs (for Envoy Gateway, its controller namespace, where it creates the Envoy proxies). Steward's API NetworkPolicy admits it. When edge.install is true, the reference install installs Envoy Gateway here. task-auth profile.

browserAuth.description: Google sign-in endpoints that Steward's apiserver calls over HTTPS (port 443) for the OIDC code exchange, discovery and keys (Steward's networkPolicy.browserAuthEgressCidrs). Google publishes no stable ranges for them, so the operator maintains this list (apelogic-ai/steward#152). browser-admin profile.

githubApi.description: GitHub API, for GitHub source retrieval and runners. Reserved for governed mode.

identityIssuer.description: github-oidc-exchange public issuer, when it is outside the cluster. Reserved for governed mode.

publicEndpoints.description: Public HTTPS origins and issuer URLs. Several charts must carry the exact same string, so each is set once here.

steward.description: Steward API origin: Steward's task-token resource (taskIdentity.resource), the edge hostname of Steward's API routes, and the steward-run API URL. task-auth profile. In the browser-admin profile it is also the browser origin (browserAuth.google.origin), the web host and the Google OAuth redirect URI's origin.

identityIssuer.description: github-oidc-exchange issuer: its own issuer setting, Steward's taskIdentity.issuer, and the edge hostname of the exchange's routes. task-auth profile.

mintIssuer.description: Steward Mint token issuer, which mcp-gw and the inference proxy trust. Reserved for governed mode.

mcpGateway.description: mcp-gw origin: Steward's MCP gateway endpoint and connections origin. Reserved for governed mode.

audiences.description: Token audiences that an issuer and its verifiers must agree on.

taskApi.description: Task tokens issued by github-oidc-exchange (config.outputAudience) and accepted by Steward (taskIdentity.audience). The github-oidc-exchange 0.7.5 chart fixes it to steward-task-api. task-auth profile.

mint.description: Mint tokens accepted by mcp-gw and the inference proxy. Reserved for governed mode.

mintSvid.description: SPIFFE SVIDs presented to Mint. Reserved for governed mode.

mintControlPlane.description: Steward control-plane tokens presented to Mint. Reserved for governed mode.

edge.description: The HTTPS edge (Gateway API) in front of Steward's task API and the github-oidc-exchange issuer. task-auth profile.

install.description: Install the BOM-pinned Gateway API CRDs and Envoy Gateway into networkPolicy.edgeNamespace. Set false when the cluster already runs a Gateway API implementation that supports BackendTLSPolicy.

gateway.description: The Gateway whose HTTPS listener serves both public hostnames.

source.description: evaluation: the reference install creates an Envoy Gateway GatewayClass and this Gateway, with a listener certificate from a self-signed edge CA (evaluation purpose only; needs edge.install and the evaluation Steward CA). operator: the routes attach to the operator's existing Gateway.

listener.description: The listener (sectionName) that terminates HTTPS for both hostnames.

clientCidrs.description: Source addresses of the edge data plane as github-oidc-exchange sees them; its NetworkPolicy admits only these (the chart's networkPolicy.ingressCidrs). On kind, the pod subnet.

stewardBackendCaConfigMap.description: ConfigMap in the Steward namespace whose ca.crt is the public CA that verifies the Steward API certificate. The edge's BackendTLSPolicy references it. The evaluation Gateway creates it from the evaluation CA; otherwise the operator's trust distribution (for example trust-manager) must publish it.

identityExchange.description: github-oidc-exchange settings that no other chart shares. The policy ConfigMap and keyring Secret are operator-owned: the chart only references them. task-auth profile.

githubAudience.description: Audience that GitHub Actions OIDC tokens must carry to be exchanged (the chart's config.githubExchangeAudience). Clients read it from the issuer's discovery metadata.

policy.description: The exchange policy. v6 issues steward-task-v3 tokens, which need Steward's federated subjects; the generator turns them on for v6.

configMapName.description: ConfigMap in namespaces.identityExchange with the policy at key policy.json.

revision.description: Change it whenever the policy ConfigMap changes; the exchange reads the policy only at startup.

secretName.description: Secret in namespaces.identityExchange with the keyring at key keyring.json.

revision.description: Change it whenever the keyring Secret changes.

publicJwksConfigMap.description: ConfigMap in the Steward namespace with the exchange's public JWKS (keyring-tool export-jwks), which Steward verifies task tokens against (taskIdentity.publicJwksConfigMap). Steward does not fetch the issuer's JWKS; publish every overlapping key here before the exchange signs with it.

spiffe.description: Workload identity. Reserved for governed mode.

trustDomain.description: SPIFFE trust domain shared by SPIRE, Steward Mint and github-oidc-exchange workload exchange.

browserAuth.description: Steward's browser login: Google Workspace OIDC, one hosted domain. The browser origin is publicEndpoints.steward. browser-admin profile.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID of a Google Cloud "Web application" client (Steward's browserAuth.google.clientId). Not secret.

workspaceDomain.description: The Google Workspace hosted domain (hd) whose users may sign in (Steward's browserAuth.google.workspaceDomain). Personal Google accounts carry no hosted domain and are rejected.

organizationId.description: Steward organization ID: a Steward-chosen stable namespace, not a Google or cloud organization ID. Same rule as the Steward 0.3.11 chart schema: 5 to 64 characters, org_ followed by 1 to 60 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, _ or -.

clientSecret.description: Existing Secret in the Steward namespace whose key holds the OAuth client secret as one raw value, no trailing newline (Steward's browserAuth.google.clientSecret). The operator creates it.

administration.description: Steward browser administration settings. browser-admin profile.

capabilityCatalog.description: Steward's deployment-owned capability catalog (config.apiserver.capabilityCatalog), passed through unchanged and validated by the Steward chart's schema. Descriptive availability for the template editor, never authority. Steward refuses to author an Envelope template unless the catalog lists at least one model. Without it the chart default (an empty catalog) applies.

registry.description: Registry mirror override, for installs that pull every artifact from the operator's own mirror (docs/registry-mirroring.md). Each artifact class that is set is pulled from its mirror; a class that is not set is pulled from upstream, as the BOM names it. An override rewrites only the registry or host and the leading path of a reference. Tags, and the digests the install pins, stay exactly the BOM's; scripts/mirror-list.sh lists the pairs to copy. Credentials are referenced by name, never given as values.

productImages.description: Images of the platform products (products.<name>.images): Steward and github-oidc-exchange, and steward-run and mcp-gw in the mirror list. Steward's chart takes one repository for all its images, which the rewrite keeps.

productCharts.description: Helm charts of the platform products (products.<name>.chart).

dependencyImages.description: Images of the external dependencies (dependencies.<name>.images): cert-manager, Envoy Gateway and the evaluation PostgreSQL.

dependencyCharts.description: Helm charts of the external dependencies (dependencies.<name>.chart): cert-manager and Envoy Gateway. Envoy Gateway's CRDs, which the Flux output takes from its chart artifact (fluxSource.chart), come from this mirror too.

gitSources.description: Git repositories the Flux output reads: the Gateway API CRDs (the fluxSource.git of their BOM manifest) and charts/steward-edge from this repository at the platform tag. The GitRepository still pins the BOM commit, or the platform tag.

manifests.description: HTTPS downloads of the CRD manifests the helmfile server-side applies (dependencies.<name>.manifests[].url). scripts/apply-manifests.sh still checks each download against its BOM SHA-256.

imagePullSecrets.description: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secrets that the workloads of the BOM charts pull with: Steward, cert-manager, github-oidc-exchange and Envoy Gateway (its controller and its Envoy proxies). The operator creates each one in every namespace those charts install into; the generator only references them.

allOf.description: The task-auth and browser-admin profiles need the edge, the public endpoints and the exchange settings.
The core profile has no edge and no exchange.
The browser-admin profile needs browser login and its egress CIDRs.
Production never uses the evaluation pieces.

With artifacts.source built, the built-artifacts lock names the final location of every product chart and image. A registry mirror rewrite of the product classes (registry.productImages, registry.productCharts) would move them a second time, so it is refused; registry settings for the other classes compose with built artifacts.

httpsOriginOnly.description: Exact HTTPS origin: scheme and host, with no port, path or trailing slash. It doubles as an edge hostname.

httpsOrigin.description: Exact HTTPS origin or issuer URL, without a trailing slash.

ociPrefix.description: An OCI registry and optional leading path, without a scheme or trailing slash, for example registry.example.test/steward-platform. The registry is a host with a dot, or localhost, and an optional port.

urlPrefix.description: An HTTPS URL without a trailing slash, for example https://git.example.test/mirrors.

keepSourceHost.description: false (the default): the prefix replaces the upstream registry or host, so ghcr.io/apelogic-ai/steward becomes <prefix>/apelogic-ai/steward. true: the upstream host is kept as the first path segment under the prefix, <prefix>/ghcr.io/apelogic-ai/steward, which never collides across upstreams.

flux.description: How the Flux OCIRepository objects of this class authenticate to the mirror (https://fluxcd.io/flux/components/source/ocirepositories/). The helmfile uses Helm's registry credentials instead (docs/registry-mirroring.md).

secretRef.description: A kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret in flux-system, for spec.secretRef.

provider.description: spec.provider: the cloud identity the source controller authenticates with (aws, azure, gcp), or generic.

certSecretRef.description: A Secret in flux-system holding the CA (ca.crt) that verifies a mirror with a private certificate authority, for spec.certSecretRef.

allOf.description: A cloud provider authenticates by workload identity; a Secret would be ignored.

repositories.description: Exact mirror URL per upstream repository URL, for mirrors whose names do not follow a prefix. It takes precedence over prefix.

flux.description: How the Flux GitRepository objects authenticate to the mirror (https://fluxcd.io/flux/components/source/gitrepositories/).

secretRef.description: A Secret in flux-system with the Git credentials (username and password, or bearerToken), for spec.secretRef.
